::: {#def-one-way-anova}
#### One-way analysis of variance

Let $y_{j1}, \ldots, y_{jn_j}$ be the $n_j$ observations in group $j$,
for $k \ge 2$ groups with $n \eqdef \sum_{j=1}^k n_j > k$ observations in all.
Let $\bar{y}_j$ be the sample mean of group $j$
and $\bar{y}$ the sample mean of all $n$ observations.
The **between-group** and **within-group sums of squares** are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{SS}_\text{between} &\eqdef \sum_{j=1}^k n_j (\bar{y}_j - \bar{y})^2,\\
\text{SS}_\text{within} &\eqdef \sum_{j=1}^k \sum_{i=1}^{n_j} (y_{ji} - \bar{y}_j)^2.
\end{aligned}
$$

The **one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA)** F-test of
$H_0: \mu_1 = \mu_2 = \cdots = \mu_k$
against the alternative that at least two group means differ
uses the statistic

$$F \eqdef \frac{\text{SS}_\text{between} / (k - 1)}{\text{SS}_\text{within} / (n - k)}.$$

Its p-value is $\Pr(F^* \ge F)$,
where $F^*$ has the $F_{k-1,\, n-k}$ distribution (@def-f-dist).
:::

::: notes
The numerator and denominator of $F$ are called the between-group
and within-group **mean squares**.
Large values of $F$ mean that the group means are spread out
more than the variation within groups would explain.
:::
